description: Implement the function-calling bridge, permission model, and the remaining error handling in orchestrator-core (P3.4, P3.5, and the orchestrator-side of P3.6), wire the CI to build/test/clippy the now-excluded mcp-client on ubuntu + windows, add minimal tauri-app resolve_permission command wiring with the mirrored TS type, and add the orchestrator-core integration test that drives a full 'model requests tool -> permission auto-allowed -> result fed back -> generation continues' loop with a mock provider + the fixture MCP server. Depends on FEAT-001 (mcp-client public API).
steps: In orchestrator-core add a bridge module (e.g. src/tools_bridge.rs or src/mcp_bridge.rs) implementing P3.4: (a) attach_tools: given the set of connected McpServerHandles, collect their visible_tools() as providers::ToolSpec and set them on ChatRequest.tools (respecting capability negotiation done elsewhere - just populate the field). (b) resolve a model tool call: given a providers::ToolCall (function.name is the namespaced name, function.arguments is a JSON string), parse the namespaced name back to (server, tool) using the mcp-client helper, look up the owning McpServerHandle. (c) validate the decoded arguments against the tool's input JSON schema (use a lightweight in-crate structural validation against the ToolDescriptor.input_schema: required properties present + basic type checks; do NOT add a heavy jsonschema crate unless already permitted - keep deps minimal). (d) invoke the tool via the handle and normalize the result into a `tool` role providers::ChatMessage (ChatMessage with role=Tool, tool_call_id=the ToolCall id, content=serialized result) so the model can continue. Failures (unknown server, validation failure, invocation error, timeout) become a structured tool-error `tool` message with is_error semantics, NOT a returned Err that crashes the turn.

Implement P3.5 permission model in orchestrator-core: a permission gate that, given the server's PermissionMode (Ask/Allow/Deny) and optional per-tool overrides (a map of tool-name -> PermissionMode), decides allow/deny/prompt for a pending invocation. In Allow -> invoke immediately; Deny -> return a structured tool-error `tool` message ('permission denied'); Ask -> emit CoreEvent::PermissionRequested{request_id,server_id,tool_name,mode,rationale} on the core event channel and BLOCK until a resolve_permission decision arrives, then proceed or deny accordingly. Implement the resolve_permission mechanism: a registry (e.g. Arc<Mutex<HashMap<Uuid, oneshot::Sender<Decision>>>> or a tokio watch/oneshot per request_id) with a method resolve_permission(request_id, decision) that unblocks the awaiting invocation. Decision type: allow/deny (+ optionally remember-for-session). Keep it framework-agnostic (no Tauri dep in orchestrator-core).

Implement the orchestrator-side of P3.6: ensure invocation errors, schema-validation failures, timeouts, and server-returned errors from the bridge are all captured as structured tool-error `tool` messages (turn does not crash); confirm tools from disconnected servers are already excluded by attach_tools using visible_tools(); surface server errors via CoreEvent::McpError where appropriate.

Update orchestrator-core/src/lib.rs: replace the mcp_client::placeholder() reference in the smoke test with a reference to a real mcp-client API item (e.g. a namespacing helper or type), add the new bridge/permission modules to the module tree, and add ALPHABETICALLY-ORDERED pub use re-exports for the new public bridge/permission types. Add any new orchestrator-core deps to its Cargo.toml as concrete literals (it is excluded): it already has serde/serde_json/uuid/chrono/thiserror/tokio and path deps on providers/mcp-client/domain/persistence/routing - likely no new crates.io dep needed; if async-trait or futures is needed, pin literals matching the workspace table.

Add minimal tauri-app resolve_permission command wiring (P3.5, UI kept OUT of scope): add a #[tauri::command] pub async fn resolve_permission(state, request_id, decision) in crates/tauri-app/src/commands.rs that calls into the orchestrator-core resolve mechanism held on AppState (add the needed field to AppState in state.rs if absent, wiring it to the SessionManager/bridge). Register the command in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs's tauri::generate_handler![...] list. Follow the existing command patterns (thin wrapper + testable inner fn where the existing commands do so). Do NOT build any UI components.

Mirror any NEW serde types that cross the IPC boundary into frontend/src/types/index.ts in EXACT sync (e.g. a PermissionDecision type for resolve_permission, if introduced). Use #[serde(rename_all="camelCase")] on the Rust side and camelCase single-line TS unions if <=100 cols. If no new IPC type is introduced (decision expressed as an existing type/string), note that no TS change was needed. Do NOT alter the existing CoreEvent/PermissionRequested TS variant unless a field changes.

Add the orchestrator-core integration test (tests/ dir) driving the full P3.4/P3.5 loop with NO live network: a MOCK ChatProvider (implements providers::ChatProvider; first chat() returns an assistant message with a ToolCall for a namespaced fixture tool, second chat() returns a final assistant text message) + the FIXTURE MCP server from FEAT-001 connected over stdio. Assert: tools are attached to the ChatRequest; the tool call resolves to the fixture server; permission is AUTO-ALLOWED (PermissionMode::Allow); the tool result is appended as a `tool` message; and the (mock) generation continues to completion. Also add unit tests for: argument-schema validation FAILURE producing a structured tool-error message (P3.6), permission Deny producing a tool-error message, and Ask-mode emitting PermissionRequested + unblocking on resolve_permission.

Update .github/workflows/ci.yml: add mcp-client to the list of excluded crates in the IMPORTANT WORKSPACE ARRANGEMENT header comment (with its dep rationale: tokio/serde_json/reqwest-rustls/ring + in-crate JSON-RPC, plus its stdio fixture-server bin). Add per-manifest CI steps for mcp-client mirroring EXACTLY the providers block ordering/style: a `cargo fmt (check, mcp-client)` step near the other fmt-check steps, and `cargo build (mcp-client)` / `cargo clippy (mcp-client) -- -D warnings` / `cargo test (mcp-client)` steps in the per-crate section (place mcp-client before orchestrator-core since orchestrator-core path-depends on it). These run on the existing [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest] matrix. Do NOT re-add macOS.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator-core exposes a function-calling bridge: attach_tools populates ChatRequest.tools from connected servers' visible_tools(); a namespaced ToolCall resolves to its owning server; arguments are validated against the tool input schema; the tool is invoked and the result becomes a `tool` role ChatMessage with tool_call_id set; all failure modes become structured tool-error messages (turn never crashes).

Permission model implemented: Allow invokes; Deny yields a tool-error message; Ask emits CoreEvent::PermissionRequested and blocks until resolve_permission(request_id, decision) unblocks it. resolve_permission mechanism is framework-agnostic in orchestrator-core.
tauri-app exposes a resolve_permission #[tauri::command] registered in generate_handler![...]; AppState wires it to the core mechanism. No UI added.
Any new IPC serde type is mirrored in frontend/src/types/index.ts in exact camelCase sync (or a note that none was needed).

orchestrator-core integration test drives model-requests-tool -> auto-allowed -> result-fed-back -> generation-continues with a mock provider + fixture MCP server; unit tests cover schema-validation failure, permission Deny, and Ask-mode resolve. (Full compile/test/clippy is CI-deferred.)

.github/workflows/ci.yml has mcp-client fmt/build/clippy(-D warnings)/test steps on ubuntu-latest + windows-latest, mirroring the providers pattern, ordered before orchestrator-core; header comment updated. macOS not re-added.
orchestrator-core/src/lib.rs no longer references mcp_client::placeholder(); new re-exports alphabetically ordered.
verification: cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo build --workspace  (offline members still green; mcp-client + orchestrator-core are excluded so unaffected)

cd hybrid-orchestrator && cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/mcp-client/Cargo.toml --check && cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/orchestrator-core/Cargo.toml --check && cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/tauri-app/Cargo.toml --check  (all offline)
cd hybrid-orchestrator/frontend && NODE_OPTIONS= prettier --check .  (offline; verifies TS mirror formatting)

CI-DEFERRED (needs network, runs on ubuntu + windows): cargo build/test/clippy(-D warnings) --manifest-path for mcp-client, orchestrator-core, and tauri-app; frontend vitest. Record offline-verified vs CI-deferred in findings.
